clean_source_blocks.text: Pauline Hanson’s One Nation now the most popular political party in the country, Redbridge Group/Accent Research poll suggests. Follow today’s news live Happy Monday: Nick Visser here to take you through the news as we start off the week. Here’s what’s on deck: One Nation is the most popular political party in the country, a new survey suggests. The poll, published Monday by the Australian Financial Review, shows support for Pauline Hanson’s party has risen four points, to 31%. Labor’s primary vote is at 28% and the Coalition sits at 20%. Continue reading...

One Nation is the most popular political party in the country, a new survey suggests. The poll, published Monday by the Australian Financial Review, shows support for Pauline Hanson’s party has risen four points, to 31%. Labor’s primary vote is at 28% and the Coalition sits at 20%. Victorians are now eligible for two cost of living measures meant to help during the ongoing fuel crisis: 20% off vehicle registration and half-price public transportation until the end of the year. The state had instituted free public transport for the past two months, which ended on Sunday. ---

“While we know there’s much more to do, these numbers are encouraging signs our methodical work to secure more care for more older Australians than ever is shifting the dial,” he said. Older people told us they want care they can trust, close to home and at a fair price. We have listened, and Labor’s getting things moving in the right direction to ensure every older Australian can get the care they deserve, sooner. Happy Monday: Nick Visser here to take you through the news as we start off the week. Here’s what’s on deck:

In three credible post-budget polls, One Nation is up one to three points, with their victory at the May 9 Farrer byelection probably also contributing. Labor took a hit in Freshwater and Resolve, but not Newspoll. Despite the hit in Resolve, they are still comfortably ahead, but Freshwater has a 50–50 tie between Labor and the Coalition. The total vote for the Coalition and One Nation was up two points to 47% in both Newspoll and Resolve, but it was up three points to 51% in Freshwater. Angus Taylor led Anthony Albanese as preferred PM in Freshwater and Resolve, but Albanese retained a clear lead in Newspoll. In Newspoll’s history of budget polling, this budget is the second worst on economic impact and the third worst on personal impact.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Aged care waiting times coming down, Labor says

Amid persistent delays and funding challenges, some aged care wait times have started coming down, according to the federal government.

The aged care minister, Sam Rae, said every person classified as urgent priority for the Support at Home program is getting funding within one month.

High-priority case wait times have dropped by a fortnight to between one and two months while medium-priority wait times have dropped from between eight and nine months to between six and seven months. Standard priority cases currently wait seven to eight months, down from 10 to 11 months in November last year.

Rae said the median wait for an assessment is consistently under one month, and the time for in-hospital assessments remains under one day.

“While we know there’s much more to do, these numbers are encouraging signs our methodical work to secure more care for more older Australians than ever is shifting the dial,” he said.

Older people told us they want care they can trust, close to home and at a fair price. We have listened, and Labor’s getting things moving in the right direction to ensure every older Australian can get the care they deserve, sooner.

Happy Monday: Nick Visser here to take you through the news as we start off the week. Here’s what’s on deck:

One Nation is the most popular political party in the country, a new survey suggests. The poll, published Monday by the Australian Financial Review, shows support for Pauline Hanson’s party has risen four points, to 31%. Labor’s primary vote is at 28% and the Coalition sits at 20%.

Victorians are now eligible for two cost of living measures meant to help during the ongoing fuel crisis: 20% off vehicle registration and half-price public transportation until the end of the year. The state had instituted free public transport for the past two months, which ended on Sunday.

---

[Lähde: The Conversation]
In three credible post-budget polls, One Nation is up one to three points, with their victory at the May 9 Farrer byelection probably also contributing. Labor took a hit in Freshwater and Resolve, but not Newspoll.

Despite the hit in Resolve, they are still comfortably ahead, but Freshwater has a 50–50 tie between Labor and the Coalition.

The total vote for the Coalition and One Nation was up two points to 47% in both Newspoll and Resolve, but it was up three points to 51% in Freshwater. Angus Taylor led Anthony Albanese as preferred PM in Freshwater and Resolve, but Albanese retained a clear lead in Newspoll.

In Newspoll’s history of budget polling, this budget is the second worst on economic impact and the third worst on personal impact.

In state politics, Labor has narrowly held the Queensland seat of Stafford at a byelection, but there was a 4% two-party swing to the LNP.

A national Newspoll, conducted May 14–17 from a sample of 1,252, gave Labor 31% of the primary vote (steady since the mid-April Newspoll), One Nation 27% (up three), the Coalition 20% (down one), the Greens 12% (down one) and all Others 10% (down one).

Labor would lead the Coalition by about 54–46 if 2025 election preference flows were applied to the primary votes, a 0.5-point gain for the Coalition.

Albanese’s net approval was steady at -17, with 57% dissatisfied and 40% satisfied.  Taylor’s net approval was up one point to -12 (48% dissatisfied, 36% satisfied).  Albanese led Taylor as better PM by 46–38 (46–37 previously).

Newspoll has asked three questions after every budget since 1988: whether the budget was good or bad for the economy, good or bad for you personally and whether the opposition would have delivered a better budget.

This budget’s economic net score of -25 (47% bad, 22% good) is the second worst, behind only 1993’s -42. The personal impact net score of -41 (52% worse off, 11% better off) was the third worst, behind -70 in 1993 and -64 in 2014.

However, by 47–39 respondents thought the Coalition would not have delivered a better budget. This score is about par for Labor governments and explains why the government didn’t take a hit on voting intentions.

By 48–9, respondents thought this budget would make inflation worse rather than better (38–14 after the 2024 budget). By 39–7, they thought they would pay more tax rather than less.

This is a graph of Albanese’s net approval in Newspoll with a smoothed line.

payload.title: Kysely nostaa One Nationin Australian suosituimmaksi puolueeksi
payload.summary: Uusi mielipidemittaus näyttää Pauline Hansonin One Nationille selvää nousua Australiassa. Samalla Victorian osavaltiossa päättyi kahden kuukauden ilmainen joukkoliikenne, ja tilalle tuli määräaikaisia kustannustukia.
payload.content:
Pauline Hansonin johtama One Nation on noussut tuoreen Redbridge Groupin ja Accent Researchin kyselyn mukaan Australian suosituimmaksi puolueeksi. Australian Financial Review’n maanantaina julkaisemassa mittauksessa puolueen kannatus on noussut neljä prosenttiyksikköä 31 prosenttiin, kun työväenpuolue Labor on 28 prosentissa ja oppositiokoalitio 20 prosentissa.

## One Nation vahvistuu kyselyissä

Mittaus on poikkeuksellisen vahva tulos One Nationille, joka on Australian politiikassa pitkään profiloitunut oikeistopopulistisena ja maahanmuuttokriittisenä puolueena. Kyselyn perusteella puolue olisi nyt ensisijaisessa puoluekannatuksessa Laborin edellä ja selvästi koalitiota vahvempi.

Laajempi kyselykuva viittaa siihen, että One Nation on ollut nousussa myös muissa budjetin jälkeisissä mittauksissa. The Conversationin mukaan kolmessa uskottavana pidetyssä kyselyssä puolue on vahvistunut yhdestä kolmeen prosenttiyksikköä. Nousua on voinut tukea myös puolueen voitto Farrerissa 9. toukokuuta järjestetyssä täytevaalissa.

Laborin asema näyttää samaan aikaan vaihtelevan mittauksesta riippuen. Freshwaterin ja Resolven kyselyissä puolue kärsi takaiskua, mutta Newspollissa vastaavaa pudotusta ei nähty. Freshwaterin mittaus näytti Laborin ja koalition olevan tasoissa kahden puolueen vertailussa, kun taas muissa kyselyissä asetelma oli Laborille suotuisampi.

## Victoriassa ilmaiset matkat päättyivät

Australiassa seurataan myös Victorian osavaltion kustannustukia. Osavaltiossa kahden kuukauden ajan voimassa ollut ilmainen joukkoliikenne päättyi sunnuntaina. Sen tilalle asukkaille on tarjolla kaksi elinkustannuksiin liittyvää helpotusta polttoainekriisin keskellä.

Victoriassa ajoneuvojen rekisteröinnistä saa 20 prosentin alennuksen, ja joukkoliikenteen liput ovat puoleen hintaan vuoden loppuun saakka. Toimet on esitetty keinona lieventää kotitalouksien menoja tilanteessa, jossa liikkumisen kustannukset ovat nousseet poliittisesti näkyväksi kysymykseksi.

Samaan aikaan liittovaltion politiikassa puolueiden kannatuskehitys voi lisätä painetta sekä Laborille että koalitiolle. Kyselyt eivät vielä ratkaise vaaliasetelmia, mutta ne kertovat One Nationin vahvistuneesta asemasta ja siitä, että talous- ja elinkustannuskysymykset pysyvät Australian politiikan keskiössä.
summary_bullets: Redbridge Groupin ja Accent Researchin kysely nostaa One Nationin 31 prosentin kannatukseen.
Laborin ensisijainen kannatus on kyselyssä 28 prosenttia ja koalition 20 prosenttia.
Victoriassa kahden kuukauden ilmainen joukkoliikenne päättyi sunnuntaina.
Osavaltio tarjoaa vuoden loppuun asti puoleen hintaan joukkoliikennettä ja 20 prosentin alennuksen ajoneuvojen rekisteröinnistä.

In Newspoll’s history of budget polling, this budget is the second worst on economic impact and the third worst on personal impact.
